name: Barbara J Kahl

positions.statement: On her campaign platform, Kahl says she would cut red tape and lower costs for Oregon small businesses.
positions.excerpt: Cutting red tape and lowering costs so Oregon small businesses can grow, hire, and compete.

positions.statement: On her campaign platform, Kahl says she supports expanding housing supply at every price point and streamlining permitting.
positions.excerpt: expanding housing supply at every price point, streamlining permitting so projects don't die in bureaucratic delay

positions.statement: On her campaign platform, Kahl says she supports local law enforcement with funding and accountability.
positions.excerpt: Supporting local law enforcement with funding and accountability — safe streets, real trust.

positions.statement: On her campaign platform, Kahl lists putting Oregon families first and lowering costs among her health care priorities.
positions.excerpt: Putting Oregon families first—lowering costs, strengthening care for our veterans

positions.statement: On her campaign platform, Kahl says she would strengthen care for veterans.
positions.excerpt: Putting Oregon families first—lowering costs, strengthening care for our veterans

positions.statement: On her campaign platform, Kahl calls for responsible forest and land stewardship that sustains the environment and timber-dependent communities.
positions.excerpt: Responsible stewardship that sustains both the environment and timber-dependent communities.

positions.statement: On her campaign platform, Kahl says she would protect working waterfronts, ports and shipping jobs.
positions.excerpt: protecting the working waterfronts, ports, and shipping jobs that move Oregon's economy.

collection_notes: Items rest on the campaign site Drkahlforcongress.com, confirmed in the candidate file via the 2026 Voters' Pamphlet. Early stop after 6 searches in a row with nothing usable. An iVoterGuide questionnaire page (ivoterguide.com) with her answers on abortion, guns, taxes, immigration, energy and others was seen but not used: it is an advocacy-group guide, not a policy-listed source. Aggregator profile pages (predictionedge) not used. Capital Chronicle guide mislabels her 'Incumbent' and shows no response from her.
